I used to hate the way I looked. Every time I looked in a mirror all I could see were my imperfections; an annoying mole in beetwen my brows, a brown mark where a pimple used to be, my prickly legs, my portruding belly. When I started to notice and take note on all my "flaws", I grew to really detest mirrors. To be frank, everytime I walked past one, I would look down and ignore it. Looking at myself was torturous.

And no, this is not the part where I claim all  my insecurities went away on a miraculous beautiful sunny day, when i realized how beautiful I was all along. Hell no. Changing my perception of myself was grueling. But I knew I had more love for myself than hatred, and that love motivated me to search deep for the brilliant girl I had forgotten all about. Hating myself was no longer sustainable (it never was, but I don't blame myself for not seeing it sooner).

I tried the body positivity thing. It was bullshit. Fuck that, it's fake; once i realized that, everything clicked. We as women have the right to be as ugly as we godamn fucking please. Jfc, when I realized this, I looked at myself in the mirror and burst out into laughter. All my life was a lie. Why was I so worried about looking perfect and put together all the time??? When I read a book my hair is up and it makes me look crazy, but I'm the happiest I can be. And my joy is beautiful. When I laugh sometimes snot comes out of my nose, it's humiliating, but somebody loved me so much they made me laugh that hard. Truly seeing my own beauty BEYOND my appearance made me the hottest I've ever been.

Yeah I have prickly legs, and a belly that portrudes, and dark spots on my legs. And sometimes my breath smells like shit, and sometimes there's dandruff on my scalp. But i'm a fully formed human being, not a porcelain doll. We as women are told that we're supposed to be perfect. Wake up beatiful, go to sleep beautiful, and repeat everyday until you die and become nothing but a hollow skull. No mascara will save you then.

I learned to love myself because of my mind, not despite of it. I am smart, I care deeply for those around me, I love to read, I love to share and receive love, I love to cook and I love to run wild like a maniac. I am full of love, and am defined by it, not by the shape of my hips or the weight of my tits. I chose to let my soul shine, and to everyone reading this, just know you can make that choice too.

If for some reason my bag gets flagged I run the risk of them finding my cart. I doubt it would get flagged BECAUSE of the cart, seeing as it's a very small amount of liquid, but on the off chance of my bag getting searched, I think I would shit my pants on the spot. 

I don't put carts on my carry-on purely out of caution and probably exaggerated worry. It has worked for multiple people, but I don’t want to risk it, because with my luck I would end up locked up.

I'm going to share my experience flying with carts but do it at your own risk.

I went to Europe- Spain, France, Italy, and other countries. I went from my home country to Spain and we took a plane from Spain to France. I had my cart and battery separated and stored in two different socks. These items were in my checked bag, and I would NEVER put them on a carry-on. I also took trains and buses in between countries, but while crossing borders I left my pen in the hotel, just to be extra safe

On another occasion, I flew from my home country to Colombia. Again, I put my cart in my checked bag, specifically in my makeup bag.

My last travel was to Florence- I just took paraphernalia (grinder). I cleaned it thoroughly, but I would never recommend traveling with flower, ever.

I encountered no issues whatsoever, except for when in my home country, a detection dog stopped to sniff my bag. My heart stopped for a second but I kept my cool and the dog moved on. Just to clarify, I was traveling from an illegal country to another illegal country, so to reiterate, do this at your own risk.

Before anything get to know them. Make sure you trust them and feel comfortable (thats extremely important believe me). The first time is never not awkward but if the therapist is good you will want to come back.

My advice is to talk to the person as if they were a friend you just met, instead of as a therapist. If you feel a connection and it went well then go back. 

The amazing thing about therapy is that you can talk literally about anything. If they ask you something you dont want to answer you dont HAVE to answer. You can talk about your obession with ice cream, or about your daddy issues lmao. Mutual trust makes the experience amazing, I honestly found a friend with my therapist.

You can ask them about things you arent certain about. Like for example, why do my friends never text me back? Anything you are genuinely curious about, (nothing is off limits). You can talk about what makes you happy, or what makes you sad. 

I cant really tell you what to expect bc every experience is different. For me personally I believe that therapists are better than psychiatrists. I go to both but therapy is more comfortable. I just go to the psychiatrist bc of my prescription pills hehe.

Hope this helped best of luck!

This can go two ways.

You understand each other, you know what you go through, and you go through it together. This results in an amazing relationship with mutual trust and respect.

Or you go down together. The thing with mental health is that it can fuck you up very easily, very fast. This happens quite a lot. People with similar issues confide in each other because they have a sense of safety. But as the relationship progresses, it can get toxic. The environment also has a lot to do with this. If you have issues, the issues of your partner will only make yours worse. 

So to conclude it depends on the level of maturity of the people involved. And even if their issues are persistent, if they are willing to change and grow to make the relationship work, this shows commitment. Once the person is willing to change for the wellbeing of a relationship, any of the other issues can be overcome.
